c.v: Table 1.4-1 provides the meaning of the characters covered in instruction descriptions.
You can find such characters and corresponding descriptions in Section

blocks.caption: Table 1.4-1. Instruction Field Names and Descriptions

c.v: In-out type (used as input/output operand). Stores address information for read/write operations, which is updated after such operations are completed.
In-out type. Temporarily stores operation results to the EE.FFT.AMS.S16.ST.INCP instruction, which will be part of the data to be written to memory.
In type (used as input operand). Stores data used to update address information.
In type. Stores data to be written to memory.
In type. Stores data involved in arithmetic operations, e.g., shifting amounts, multipliers and etc.
Out type (used as output operand). Stores results of instruction operations.
In type. Stores data used for vector operations.
Out type. Stores results of vector operations.
Out type. Stores data read from memory.
In type. Stores data to be written to memory.
general-purpose floating-point register. Stores floating-point data read from memory.
general-purpose floating-point register. Stores floating-point data to be written to memory.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 1. Used to select signals.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 3. Used to select signals.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 7. Used to select signals.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 15. Used to select signals.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 1. Represents shifting numbers.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 3. Represents shifting numbers.
immediate value ranging from 0 to 15. Represents shifting numbers.
unsigned immediate value ranging from 0 to 127 with an interval of 1. This is used to show the size of the updated read/write operation address value.
unsigned immediate value ranging from 0 to 254 with an interval of 2. This is used to show the size of the updated read/write operation address value.
signed immediate value ranging from -256 to 252 with an interval of 8. This is used to show the size of the updated read/write operation address value.
signed immediate value ranging from -2048 to 2032 with an interval of 16. This is used to show the size of the updated read/write operation address value.
signed immediate value ranging from -128 to 112 with an interval of 16. This is used to show the size of the updated read/write operation address value.
Some instructions have multiple operands with the same function.
Those operands are distinguished by adding numbers after field names.
For example, the EE.LDF.128.IP instruction has four fu registers, fu0 ~ 3.
